sentences.text: The premise holds on two consecutive quarters of filing language, and the latest quarter's segment growth runs ahead of the company's own growth, so Data Center is gaining share rather than coasting.

At 92.5% of revenue and contributing +102.5 percentage points of the +105.9% total growth, Data Center growth is close to the whole company's growth, so this claim is in effect the thesis's revenue case.
The quarterly path argues for continuing momentum: company growth sped up by 20.6 percentage points over the prior quarter, and revenue rose in each of the 8 quarters.

The step from 'still growing' to holding an overweight into the next report is not backed by the record: there is no valuation or implied-growth analytic, so whether this growth is already in the price cannot be judged here.
The record also holds an event after the newest 10-Q, the CEO's resignation with the CFO named interim CEO, whose effect on the next quarter no filing in the record can show.
Growth is not merely positive but accelerating on a quarterly basis, from +92% to +117% year over year for Data Center, which leaves a wide cushion before the claim could fail.
The Compute and Networking segment corollary holds with a margin of +113.6 points, an independent read pointing the same way.
On a fiscal-year basis Data Center growth slowed by 74.2 percentage points, so the quarterly acceleration sits inside a longer deceleration that the claim's wording hides.
Receivables grew faster than revenue, contrary to what the claim implies, with receivable days rising to 59.6 from 54.1, so part of the reported growth has not yet turned into cash.
The filing itself warns that faster product transitions may create revenue volatility, a risk that matters most for a position held through a single report.
Whether the next quarter's revenue, nearly all Data Center, keeps rising sequentially from the latest level rather than showing the volatility the filing warns of.
Whether receivable days stop climbing above the 59.6 now recorded, which would show the growth converting to cash.
How the leadership change after the newest filing shows up in the next results, which the record cannot yet address.

conditions.text: Quarterly revenue falling below the latest quarter's $96.22B would signal the Data Center-led growth stalling.
Receivables rising above $63.06B while revenue stalls would weaken the quality of the reported growth.
A results 8-K reporting a year-over-year decline in Data Center revenue would overturn the claim.
